_meta.indication: Omegaven is indicated as a source of calories and fatty acids in pediatric patients with parenteral nutrition-associated cholestasis (PNAC).

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.phase: Investigator-initiated, open-label, single-center, single-arm historically-controlled studies
pivotal_trials.design: Prospective, open-label, single-center, single-arm studies; Omegaven-treated patients pair-matched 2:1 to historical control patients receiving soybean oil-based lipid emulsion, primarily based on DBil levels and postmenstrual age at baseline.
pivotal_trials.population: Pediatric patients with PNAC (direct/conjugated bilirubin >= 2 mg/dL) who required PN for at least 14 days; Study 34 enrolled patients less than 2 years of age and Study 35 enrolled patients less than 5 years of age.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint was changes over time in body weight adjusted for age; secondary endpoints included age-adjusted body length/height and head circumference.
pivotal_trials.n: 123 patients in the pair-matched analysis population (82 Omegaven; 41 historical control); 78 from Study 34 (52; 26) and 45 from Study 35 (30; 15).
pivotal_trials.result: Median age-adjusted body weight (Z-scores) over time for Omegaven-treated patients appeared similar to historical control; full enteral feeding was achieved by 52 (63%) Omegaven and 24 (59%) historical control patients, with median time to full enteral feeding of approximately 15 weeks in both groups. Studies were not designed/powered to demonstrate noninferiority or superiority.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>5%, higher than comparator) included vomiting (46% vs 44%), agitation (35% vs 34%), bradycardia (35% vs 33%), apnea (20% vs 19%), viral infection (16% vs 10%), and erythema (12% vs 8%). Serious adverse events occurred in 81% (Omegaven) vs 82% (historical control). Warnings include risk of death in preterm infants due to pulmonary lipid accumulation, hypersensitivity, infections, fat overload syndrome, refeeding syndrome, and hypertriglyceridemia.
target_moa: A highly refined fish oil injectable emulsion containing omega-3 fatty acids (EPA and DHA) that provides a biologically utilizable source of calories and essential fatty acids; fatty acids serve as substrates for energy production (chiefly via beta oxidation) and for membrane structure and precursors of bioactive molecules.
modality: Other (highly refined fish oil triglycerides injectable lipid emulsion)

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA Advisory committee because outside expertise was not necessary and there were no controversial issues that would benefit from advisory committee discussion.

citations.quote: This section is not applicable to this NDA as the studied population was exclusively pediatrics, and the product obtained Orphan Drug Designation on 2/27/2008 for treatment of PNALD indication, then reverified on 1/25/2017 for the nutritional indication for patients with PNAC (designation #07-2515). summary.text: Omegaven (NDA 210589) was reviewed under Priority Review, had Fast Track Designation for the source of calories and fatty acids in pediatric PNAC indication, and held Orphan Drug Designation. It was approved based on two open-label historically-controlled investigator-initiated studies (Studies 34 and 35), not by accelerated approval; two postmarketing requirements were imposed.
